question: Why did the p95 latency go up on 09 March 2026?

contributing_factors.description: The flash sale campaign likely caused the spike in request volume and error rate.
why_chain: The flash sale campaign went live at the right time and place (233 minutes before the change).
This led to a significant increase in request volume, which in turn caused the autoscaler to request additional instances.
The increased request volume also led to higher error rates due to the system being overwhelmed.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The increase in latency was due to a configuration change.
ruled_out.reason: There is no evidence of a configuration change that would cause a sudden increase in latency.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The increase in latency was due to a data quality issue.
ruled_out.reason: There is no evidence of bad or unusual input data that would cause a sudden increase in latency.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The increase in latency was due to a dependency issue with an external service.
ruled_out.reason: There is no evidence of a dependency issue with an external service that would cause a sudden increase in latency.

evidence.summary: P95 latency for region ap-south rose from 137 ms to 290 ms (+112%), with a change point at 2026-03-09T09:05:00Z.
The change is concentrated in region ap-south: 4 of 12 service/region segments changed; the other segments stayed flat (largest after/before ratio 1.01).
At the same time, request volume for region ap-south rose (1230 per 5 min before, 5151 per 5 min after, +319%).
At the same time, error rate for region ap-south rose (0.41% before, 0.80% after, +96%).
Marketing: flash sale campaign goes live in ap-south at 09:05 UTC (ap-south; 233 min before the change; record R011; fit: right time and place: a strong candidate cause)
Request volume 3x normal in ap-south (ap-south; 12 min after the change; record R012; fit: after the change, so a symptom, not a cause)
autoscaler: scaling out, 4 new instances requested (ap-south; 20 min after the change; record R013; fit: after the change, so a symptom, not a cause)

reasons: ✓ A change event (tickets) lines up in time (233 min before the change).
✓ 2 log/alert record(s) after the change agree with the numbers.
✓ Request volume rose, as a traffic cause requires.
✓ No competing change event fits as well.
✓ The main factor rests on this event.

actions.action: Review and optimize the autoscaler configuration to better handle flash sale campaigns.
Implement a traffic management system to handle sudden spikes in traffic during campaigns.
Monitor request volume and error rates closely during flash sale campaigns and adjust scaling policies accordingly.
